dedupe_keys.name: openmrg commercial microwave link radar and rain gauge data for gothenburg 2015

description: OpenMRG is an open dataset of signal levels from a working mobile backhaul network, published together with weather radar and rain gauge observations for the same area so that the effect of rain on radio links can be studied. It contains transmitted and received signal levels every 10 seconds from 364 bidirectional commercial microwave links (728 sub-links) of an operator network in Gothenburg, Sweden, with their true coordinates, frequencies between 7 and 38 GHz (mostly above 25 GHz) and path lengths of 0.1 to 15 km, alongside the Swedish operational C-band radar composite and 11 municipal rain gauges, for June to August 2015. Records are almost complete: 99.99 per cent for the links, 100 per cent for the gauges and 99.6 per cent for the radar. It was released by SMHI and Ericsson and described in Earth System Science Data in December 2022; its main aim is to help researchers develop methods to estimate rainfall from link attenuation. Coverage: about 2,000 square kilometres around Gothenburg, one summer. Format and access: NetCDF and text files with Python scripts on Zenodo, free under CC BY-SA 4.0. Caveats: one city, one summer; operator and exact equipment are anonymised. Simulation uses: rain fade models for microwave backhaul, weather-dependent link performance and outage modelling, and calibration of propagation models against measurements. Related records: ITU-R propagation recommendations give the standard attenuation models these data test.
